title: Trading policy

tiers.name: ASK and Manager Personnel
tiers.description: Directors and employees of ASFML, the Abacus Group, ASOL, Abacus Group Holdings Limited and Abacus Group Projects Limited and their controlled entities.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors (and their associates), senior management, key management personnel (AASB 124) of ASFML, ASOL and subsidiaries; employees advised by the Company Secretary that they have or may have Inside Information; and any other person the Chair determines in his or her absolute discretion.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may influence or be influenced by the director/employee (spouse, de facto partner, children, dependants); investment vehicles or entities in which the person or associate is a beneficiary or has direct/indirect control (trusts, superannuation funds, companies); any other entity where they are a director, secretary or executive officer; and any investment manager acting on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into a hedging transaction to limit his or her exposure to Stapled Securities (whether received under an equity based remuneration scheme or otherwise and whether vested or unvested)

windows.end_anchor: the day after which ASK's full year results are released to the ASX
the day after which ASK's half year results are released to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: ASK may impose a restriction on trading during any period, including one that would otherwise be outside the Blackout Period, and the Board may at any time determine that a Blackout Period is extended for Restricted Persons. The Policy does not state whether such additional restrictions are confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule; Stapled Securities are defined as shares/units, not OTC derivatives. An OTC put and call limits exposure to Stapled Securities and so falls within the absolute hedging prohibition, which applies whether the underlying holding is vested or unvested and has no Chair-approval or clearance route.
rules.evidence: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge their exposure to Stapled Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban with no approval mechanism, expressly stated to apply whether the Stapled Securities were received under an equity remuneration scheme or otherwise and whether vested or unvested.
rules.evidence: If an ASK and Manager Personnel or associate enters into a hedging transaction to limit his or her exposure to Stapled Securities (whether received under an equity based remuneration scheme or otherwise and whether vested or unvested) ... For those reasons, ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge their exposure to Stapled Securities.

rules.detail: Not named. A prepaid forward or similar monetisation contract would be an indirect dealing/change in relevant interest, so it must sit outside a Blackout Period and outside possession of Inside Information; general (non-Restricted) personnel need no separate approval or notification for it.
rules.evidence: indirect acquisition where a director, employee or associate holds a relevant interest in the Stapled Securities

rules.detail: Not named, but as a dealing it triggers the Restricted Person requirement to notify the Company Secretary before any dealing at any time, including outside the Blackout Period, with the decision-maker able to direct no dealing or impose conditions without giving reasons.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify the ASK Company Secretary prior to any dealing, including periods outside of the Blackout Period as set out in rule 5.3 (including any dealing by their associates).

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Stock/securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Not named, but a CFD used to limit exposure to Stapled Securities is caught by the absolute hedging prohibition in the same way as an OTC derivative.
rules.evidence: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge their exposure to Stapled Securities.

rules.detail: Holding Stapled Securities subject to a margin loan is banned unless the Chair (or Chair of the Audit Committee if the Chair is the applicant) gives prior written approval; the Policy flags that a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period or while the borrower holds inside information may itself amount to insider trading.
rules.evidence: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from holding Stapled Securities which are subject to margin loans or similar funding arrangements unless they have prior written approval from the Chair to do so

rules.detail: 'Similar funding arrangements' extends beyond margin loans to any arrangement under which security is granted over the Stapled Securities; permitted only with prior written Chair approval.
rules.evidence: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from holding Stapled Securities which are subject to margin loans or similar funding arrangements unless they have prior written approval from the Chair to do so

rules.detail: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is a 'similar funding arrangement' to a margin loan and is permitted only with prior written Chair approval; no floor or price-trigger guidance is given, only a warning that a forced sale during a Blackout Period or while holding inside information risks constituting insider trading.
rules.evidence: Margin loans used to fund the purchase of Stapled Securities may give the lender the right to require the sale of those securities at a time during the Blackout Period ... or at a time when the borrower has knowledge of market sensitive information. Such a sale may amount to insider trading (or create a perception of insider trading).

rules.detail: No short-term or speculative trading holding-period rule is stated anywhere in the Policy.

clearance.evidence: ASK and Manager Personnel and their associates must not deal in Stapled Securities during the Blackout Periods set out in rule 5.3.

clearance.approver: Chair (for Restricted Persons who are ASK directors), the Abacus Group Managing Director (for Restricted Persons who are employees), or the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (for the Chair)
clearance.evidence: The Restricted Person will be notified within 24 hours whether they may trade or not. ... may direct the person ... not to deal, or to impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion ... Provided no direction is given or contrary condition is imposed, the Restricted Person will have five business days to enter into the proposed dealing.

clearance.approver: Chair (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee if the Chair is the applicant)
clearance.evidence: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from holding Stapled Securities which are subject to margin loans or similar funding arrangements unless they have prior written approval from the Chair to do so.

exemption_authority: Chair (or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee if the Chair is the applicant) grants Blackout Period trading approval for financial hardship, court order/enforceable undertaking, or other Chair-discretion circumstances, and separately grants prior written approval for margin loans/secured funding arrangements; approval may be given or refused without reasons, is final, and may be withdrawn if new information emerges.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute hedging ban, vested or unvested
bespoke_clauses.clause: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge their exposure to Stapled Securities [whether received under an equity based remuneration scheme or otherwise and whether vested or unvested].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's derivative legs are banned outright for everyone, at all times, with no Chair-approval or clearance mechanism at all (unlike the margin loan/secured funding regime), so the derivative component of a funded collar cannot be structured under this Policy regardless of tier or vesting status.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin loans used to fund the purchase of Stapled Securities may give the lender the right to require the sale of those securities at a time during the Blackout Period ... or at a time when the borrower has knowledge of market sensitive information. Such a sale may amount to insider trading (or create a perception of insider trading).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg is clearable with Chair approval, the Policy itself flags that the bank's or a lender's enforcement sale during a closed period or while the executive holds inside information could itself constitute insider trading, so enforcement/foreclosure mechanics need bespoke drafting and Chair sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would create a perception risk outlined above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chair can refuse to approve the loan/secured-funding leg purely on the ground it might be perceived as trading on inside information, an additional discretionary hurdle beyond the express legal tests.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must notify the ASK Company Secretary prior to any dealing, including periods outside of the Blackout Period ... Notwithstanding prior notification of a proposed dealing, the Chair ... may direct the person ... not to deal, or to impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director or KMP wanting the (permitted) loan leg must clear this notify-and-await-decision gate even outside a Blackout Period, with a discretionary veto or conditions and only a 5-business-day execution window once cleared.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this trading policy will also apply to any trading in Abacus Group securities in the same way as it applies to Stapled Securities, including restricting trading during a Blackout Period of Abacus Group
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the manager relationship means the individual also holds Abacus Group Limited securities, the same absolute hedging ban and Chair-approval-for-financing regime applies to those securities too.

summary: A funded collar cannot be implemented in full under this Policy: section 5.6 imposes an absolute, unconditional prohibition on hedging transactions over Stapled Securities, expressly covering both vested and unvested holdings, with no Chair-approval or clearance mechanism at all, so neither the purchased put nor the written call can be entered into by any ASK and Manager Personnel or their associates. The loan leg is treated differently: margin loans and 'similar funding arrangements' secured against Stapled Securities are permitted with prior written Chair approval (or Audit and Risk Committee Chair approval if the Chair is the applicant), though the Policy itself warns that a lender's forced sale during a Blackout Period or while the borrower holds inside information may amount to insider trading. Restricted Persons (directors, senior management, KMP, and anyone the Chair designates) face an additional requirement to notify the Company Secretary before any dealing at any time, with the deciding officer able to impose conditions or block the dealing without giving reasons, and any approval can still be refused solely on perception-of-insider-trading grounds. Because the hedging ban is absolute and carries no exception or clearance route, the funded collar structure as a whole is not achievable under this Policy even though the secured loan component alone could, in principle, be cleared.
